title: Argo CD bootstrap inputs and ownership, v1alpha1
description: The inputs and the ownership rules for the Argo CD installation that V2 uses as its GitOps controller: the pinned release, install manifest and images, the namespace, each object the manifest declares and the ownership row that holds it, the privileges the installation needs and grants, the refusals, and the scoped removal. One repository procedure implements it: it installs, verifies, and removes the installation on a cluster the operator selects and the procedure verifies. It was executed on one provider, docker-desktop. It was not executed on kind. This procedure creates no Application. Since 2026-10-04 another procedure applies one Application and its project, which ADR 0019 decided. Every rule states what enforces it and what that check does not establish.

procedure.applyMechanism: kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts, with the verified manifest file, unmodified, into the namespace argocd
procedure.manifestSource: Downloaded from the pinned source URL into the ignored directory .artifacts/argocd-bootstrap/, or read from a file the operator names with --manifest. Either is used only when its SHA-256 is the pinned value. The file is hashed a second time immediately before the apply.
procedure.imageDigestMechanismStatement: The manifest is applied unmodified and names each image by tag. After the rollout, the procedure reads the image identity that each container status reports, init containers included, and compares it with the pinned digest. A container that the record does not list, or that reports no identity, fails the check. ADR 0017 D5 is kept: the applied bytes are the verified bytes.
procedure.idempotence: A second install on an installation that carries the marker and records the pinned SHA-256 applies the same bytes again with the same field manager. It does not create or relabel the namespace.
procedure.marker: The label and the annotation together. The procedure writes both in one request, so it refuses a namespace that carries the label and records no SHA-256.

runs.result: failed at the download, three times, and changed nothing in the cluster
passed, with the procedure as the first commit of the implementing change stored it
passed, with the procedure as the independent review left it

pinnedInputs.howObserved: The install manifest was downloaded twice over HTTPS, once by the tag and once by the commit the tag names. Both downloads have the SHA-256 recorded here. Each image digest is the Docker-Content-Digest header that the image's registry returned for the tag the manifest names. No signature, attestation, or provenance document was verified.

installManifest.appliedStatement: Applied on the docker-desktop provider on 2026-10-03, six times in two passing runs: in each run a first install, a second install on the same installation, and an install after a removal. Not applied on kind.

testedKubernetesMinors.source: docs/operator-manual/tested-kubernetes-versions.md in the upstream repository at the pinned commit, the row for Argo CD 3.5

namespace.name: argocd
namespace.whyThisName: The manifest declares no Namespace and writes no namespace on its namespaced objects. Its one ClusterRoleBinding names a ServiceAccount in the namespace argocd. An unmodified manifest therefore binds the application controller only when it is applied into that namespace.

runtimeCreatedObjects.createdBy: the secret-init init container of the argocd-redis Deployment, through the argocd-redis Role
runtimeCreatedObjects.basis: The runs on docker-desktop listed the Secrets in the namespace by name after the install, and argocd-redis was one of them. That the object exists is observed. What creates it is still read from the Role and the manifest, and was not observed. Its value was not read.

runtimeCreatedObjects.createdBy: the ApplicationSet controller, for leader election, through the argocd-applicationset-controller Role
runtimeCreatedObjects.basis: The argocd-applicationset-controller Role grants create on leases and names this lease. The run on docker-desktop listed the Leases in the namespace after the install and found none, so the object stays inferred and unobserved.

runtimeCreatedObjectsObserved: The run also listed configmap/kube-root-ca.crt, which Kubernetes creates in every namespace and the bootstrap does not own.

componentsNotInstalled.consequence: No Argo CD API, no web interface, and no login credential exists. Reconciliation state is read from the Application objects with kubectl.

componentsInstalledAndUnused.reason: The core-install manifest includes it, and the manifest is applied unmodified so that one SHA-256 identifies what was applied. InferOps creates no ApplicationSet object, so the controller has nothing to reconcile.

sharedKindBoundaries.statement: Terraform owns the platform namespace. The bootstrap owner owns the namespace argocd. The two names differ, and neither owner creates, labels, or deletes the other's namespace.

Every namespaced object the bootstrap owner creates is in the namespace argocd. A Helm release installs into the platform namespace and never into argocd. The boundary does not cover an object of an argoproj.io kind: one Application and one AppProject are also in argocd, and the bootstrap owner does not own them. Since 2026-10-04 the Application procedure owns them, as the row argocd-workload-application.

bootstrapOperator.statement: The credential the bootstrap procedure acts through must be able to create a Namespace, three CustomResourceDefinitions, one ClusterRole and one ClusterRoleBinding, and the namespaced objects the manifest declares. Kubernetes refuses to create a ClusterRole that grants more than its creator holds, and this ClusterRole grants every verb on every resource. The credential therefore needs cluster-admin, or an equivalent grant.
bootstrapOperator.basis: Read from the manifest and from the Kubernetes rule against privilege escalation. The run on docker-desktop used that provider's administrator credential, and the apply succeeded. No run tried a narrower credential, so the lower bound stays inferred.

grantedToArgoCd.name: argocd-application-controller
grantedToArgoCd.consequence: The application controller can read and change every object in the cluster, including the objects Terraform owns and the bootstrap owner's own objects. The grant is the upstream default and is not narrowed by this record.

refusals.condition: No provider is selected, or the selected cluster does not pass the provider's identity checks.
The SHA-256 of the manifest bytes is not the pinned SHA-256.
The minor version the selected cluster's server reports is not one of the pinned tested minors.

A namespace named argocd exists without the bootstrap lifecycle marker, or with the marker label and no recorded manifest SHA-256. Or no marked namespace exists while an Argo CD CustomResourceDefinition, or a ClusterRole or ClusterRoleBinding named argocd-application-controller, does. Removal also refuses when no namespace named argocd exists.
A marked namespace records a manifest SHA-256 that is not the pinned SHA-256. An upgrade in place is not decided.
An Application, ApplicationSet, or AppProject object exists in any namespace.

removal.statement: Removal deletes what the bootstrap owner created, and nothing else. It is not part of any other teardown operation. It deletes by the kinds and names this record lists, so it needs no download. It was executed four times on the docker-desktop provider on 2026-10-03, in two runs, with no Application present, and each time no listed object remained. The refusal for an existing Application was executed against stubs only.
steps: Select and verify the target cluster, as for every mutation.
Refuse unless a namespace named argocd exists and carries the bootstrap lifecycle marker.
Refuse when an Application, ApplicationSet, or AppProject object exists.
Delete the StatefulSet and the three Deployments in the namespace argocd, and wait until no Argo CD pod remains.
Refuse again when an Application, ApplicationSet, or AppProject object exists.
Delete the three CustomResourceDefinitions, the ClusterRole, and the ClusterRoleBinding, by the names this record lists.
Delete the namespace argocd, which removes the remaining namespaced objects.
Confirm that no Argo CD CustomResourceDefinition, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, or namespace remains.
doesNotTouch: the platform namespace, its metadata, and the model cache claim
a Helm release or any object in the platform namespace
images that the node's container runtime pulled
removal.whyCustomResourcesBlockRemoval: Deleting a CustomResourceDefinition deletes every object of that kind. An Application that carries a resource finalizer deletes the workload objects it manages when it is deleted while the controller runs. Removal of the controller must not remove a workload. The controllers are stopped before the definitions are deleted, and the check is repeated between the two, because an object created after the first check would otherwise be deleted with its definition.
knownGaps: The two checks and the deletions are not atomic. An object created after the second check is deleted with its definition.
An object that carries a finalizer and is created after the controllers stop keeps its definition and the namespace in a terminating state. No recovery is decided.
A second Argo CD in another namespace uses the same definitions. Removal does not detect it when it holds no Application.
When a person deletes the namespace argocd by hand, the bootstrap and the removal both refuse. The recovery is manual and is not decided.

outOfScope: a workload Application, an AppProject, or a desired-state directory
a second cluster or a cluster registered with Argo CD
the Argo CD API server, web interface, single sign-on, and notifications

rules.statement: Every kind that the bootstrap owner shares with Terraform or with Helm has a declared boundary, and no cluster-scoped kind is shared.
rules.limit: The test compares kinds in the ownership inventory with the boundaries this record declares. It compares kinds and not objects. A second test, test_the_namespace_is_not_one_another_owner_holds, compares the namespace name with the Terraform default and the two namespace constants. Both read files and no cluster.

rules.statement: Neither the committed chart render nor the Terraform configuration declares a cluster-scoped kind that the bootstrap owner owns, and neither targets the namespace argocd.
rules.limit: The test reads the two committed renders and the Terraform files as text. It does not read a values file or a namespace flag that a caller supplies at install time, or a template branch that the committed renders do not take. A Terraform kubernetes_manifest resource hides its kind from the test.

rules.statement: Argo CD does not create, upgrade, or remove its own installation, and it reconciles no object that the bootstrap owner or Terraform owns.
rules.limit: Until 2026-10-04 this rule was held by an absence: no Argo CD custom resource was committed. ADR 0019 added one Application and its project, and the test now reads them. The project admits one destination namespace, which is not argocd, eight namespaced kinds, and no cluster-scoped kind. So the one Application is refused the installation, the definitions, the cluster role, a Namespace, and a claim. A second test holds that no other tracked file declares an Argo CD custom resource. The tests read files. They do not narrow the grant of the application controller, and they do not see an Application that a person creates in the cluster by hand.

rules.statement: InferOps commits no ApplicationSet object, no app-of-apps Application, and no Argo CD cluster registration.
rules.limit: The test reads every tracked file except two suites that quote a custom resource. It holds that the two manifests of ADR 0019 are the only tracked files that declare an Argo CD custom resource, that neither is an ApplicationSet, and that no file registers a cluster. The source of the one Application is the chart and not a directory of Applications, and another suite holds that. A manifest that a template assembles from parts is not matched. It reads no cluster.

rules.statement: No InferOps component that serves a request addresses Argo CD.
rules.limit: The test reads every tracked file under the serving directories for a reference to Argo CD, and refuses a build file that names it beside the two procedures and the two manifests. It does not establish that a request is served while Argo CD is absent or stopped; no run has measured that, and no release was installed during the bootstrap run. Not being on the request path is not the same as being unable to affect serving: while the Application is applied, a running controller can change, restart, or delete serving objects, and its containers compete for the node without a request or a limit.

rules.statement: The manifest is addressed by commit and SHA-256, and each image by digest. No pin is a branch, a tag alone, or a floating version.
rules.limit: The test checks the form of each pin and that the pins agree with one another. It contacts no network, so it does not establish that upstream still serves these bytes.

rules.statement: The bootstrap and the removal run the selected provider's identity checks before their first mutation, and neither creates, enables, resets, reconfigures, or deletes a cluster.
rules.limit: The test executes the procedure against stub tools, for each of the three operations, and reads the calls it made: no mutation ran, and the installation was not read before the target was verified. Three more tests refuse no provider, an unsupported provider, and a kind target with no cluster name; the runs repeated those three with the real tools, and each was refused before any cluster was contacted. No run refused a wrong cluster. A static test holds the one call to inferops::resolve_target ahead of the first cluster read. The guard's own limits are the provider contract's: a cluster the operator deliberately gave the selected provider's shape passes it.

rules.statement: The bootstrap computes the SHA-256 of the manifest bytes, downloaded or supplied, and refuses before its first mutation when it is not the pinned value. It computes it again immediately before the apply. The removal reads no manifest.
rules.limit: The test executes the procedure against stub tools with a file that is not the pin, and a second test does the same with a download. The stub download is a shell script. It did not reproduce the defect that the first run on Windows exposed, where the real curl could not write to an unconverted path. A SHA-256 identifies bytes and does not authenticate them.

rules.statement: The bootstrap does not report success unless every Argo CD container, init containers included, runs the pinned digest of its image at that moment.
rules.limit: The test executes the verify operation against stub tools with five wrong container reports. A second test executes the install operation with a wrong report, with sha256sum also replaced by a stub, because a test cannot hold bytes with the pinned SHA-256. The runs on docker-desktop executed the passing comparison only. The check keys on the container name: a pod that reports no container status yet is not seen when another pod reports the same name, and a failed pod left in the namespace fails the check. The unmodified manifest names each image by tag, and four containers set imagePullPolicy Always. A pod that restarts later resolves the tag again and can run other bytes. The rule covers the moment of the check and nothing after it.

rules.statement: The bootstrap and the removal refuse an Argo CD installation that this bootstrap did not create, and never adopt one.
rules.limit: The test executes the procedure against stub tools. Further tests refuse each of the five cluster-scoped objects when no marked namespace exists, refuse a namespace that carries the label and records no SHA-256, and refuse the removal of an unmarked or absent namespace. No run met a foreign installation in a cluster; the one refusal of this kind that a run produced was a removal with no namespace. The marker is a label and an annotation on the namespace. A person who can change a namespace can set both. The five cluster-scoped objects carry no marker: when a marked namespace exists, the install does not check whose they are, and server-side apply with --force-conflicts takes over one that another party replaced.

rules.statement: Removal deletes only the objects of the bootstrap owner, and refuses while an Application, ApplicationSet, or AppProject object exists.
rules.limit: The test executes the removal against stub tools, once for each of the three kinds. Further tests hold the order of the ten deletions, hold each deletion to a named object, hold the wait for the pods and the wait for the namespace, and refuse an unanswered pod query. A static suite refuses a deletion that is not one of the six exact commands. The runs on docker-desktop removed the installation four times with no Application present. On 2026-10-04 each of three runs of the Application procedure on docker-desktop executed the removal while the Application and its project existed. Each time it refused at its first check and deleted nothing. It refused before it stopped a controller. The second check, after the controllers stop, is executed against stubs only. No test reaches a time limit, and no call sets a request timeout, so an API server that stops answering holds a read. The record lists four gaps in the order.

rules.statement: The security baseline holds threat, control, and risk rows for the Argo CD installation, written before the first install.
rules.limit: The test establishes that the rows exist and that each guard they name is a function of the procedure. It cannot establish that the rows were written before the first install. The record of the run states that order, and nothing checks it.

rules.statement: No InferOps record derives a caller outcome from the sync state or the health state that Argo CD reports.
rules.limit: Nothing records Argo CD state yet. Review alone holds this rule.

doesNotEstablish: that Argo CD reconciles anything; this procedure creates no Application, and the record of the Application procedure's run is a separate record
that the procedure installs or removes Argo CD on the kind provider; it was executed on docker-desktop only, and one provider's run certifies no other
that upstream still serves the pinned bytes after the run, or that a pinned image is free of known vulnerabilities; neither image was scanned
that the pinned release or images are authentic; no signature was verified
that a request is served while Argo CD is absent or stopped; no release was installed during the run
that the order avoids a stuck deletion; every completed removal ran with no Application, and the three removals with an Application present refused at their first check
that a container runs the pinned image after a later restart
that the core profile reconciles an Application on kind; on docker-desktop it reconciled one Application in a committed project, in the Application procedure's run
that the host has the capacity to run Argo CD beside a release under load; the Application procedure's run held one release beside it and measured nothing
that a credential narrower than cluster-admin can run the bootstrap
